question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides the procedure for impeachment of the President?
solution:
The correct answer is __**​Article 61**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ARTICLE 61(Procedure For Impeachment of The President):**

 
 
• When a President is to be impeached for violation of the Constitution, the charge shall be preferred by either House of Parliament.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/efb90c3647c276e117dc17fb6439410dad00fafe8f511a89c38f32cba7de65df.png] 

 
• The ​President of India:

 
 
• The President of India is the head of the Indian State. 
 
• The President of India is the first citizen of India and acts as the symbol of unity, integrity, and harmony.
 
 
 
• The Chief Justice of India: Chief Justice of the Republic of India and chief judge of the Supreme Court of India on top of the important officer of the Indian federal judiciary.
 
 
• At present **Dr Justice Dhananjaya Y Chandrachud** is the 50th Chief Justice of India.
 
 
 
• The Law Commission:
 
 
• ​Law Commission of India is neither a constitutional body nor a constitutional body.
 
• It is a decision-making body recognized by the Government of India and Its major purpose is to work for legal reforms.
 
• The Commission is recognized for a permanent tenure and works as an advisory body to the Ministry of Law and Justice and its membership primarily includes legal experts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 70 (Discharge of President Function in other contingencies):**

 
 
• ​Parliament may make such provision as it thinks fit for the discharge of the functions of the President in any contingency not provided for in this Chapter.
 
 
 
• Article 77:
 
 
• The President shall establish rules for the most convenient transaction of Indian government affairs and the distribution of such affairs among ministers.​
